title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: preliminaries to 'chirurgie conforme', the cutting and gluing of conformal (Riemann) surfaces along boundary circles. The next page (11.1.84) starts the formal treatment of conformal surfaces with boundary. This page sets up a linear-algebra dictionary for the boundary circles and for the gluing data.

(1) Dictionary. A 'cercle torique' is a circle carrying the structure of a torsor under the rotation group (marginal note: a torsor under a topological group isomorphic to R/Z, i.e. U = S^1 up to orientation). The page gives these correspondences:
- cercles toriques ↔ real Euclidean vector planes ↔ unitary complex lines, isomorphic to C but not canonically.
- Oriented toric circles ↔ oriented Euclidean planes ↔ unitary complex lines T. The Hermitian form gives T ≅ T̄^∨, i.e. T^∨ ≅ T̄.
- U-torsors ↔ complex lines T equipped with a 'jauge' D. A jauge is a unit disc, i.e. a norm, i.e. a conformal gauge. The torsor is the boundary ∂D.

(2) NB on gauges. For a fixed complex line D, the set J(D) of gauges is (D∖0)/U. It is an R_{>0}-torsor. Duality gives an anti-isomorphism of R_{>0}-torsors J(D) → J(D^∨) (≅ J(D̄)): a disc goes to its polar disc, so scaling by r becomes scaling by 1/r.

(3) Isom(C'^-, C'') ≅ Isom(C''^-, C'). Orientation-reversing identifications of two oriented toric circles correspond bijectively under inversion. Passing to the oppositely oriented ('dual') toric circle corresponds to passing from T to the dual complex line T^∨ ≅ T̄.

(4) Main statement. Let T', T'' be complex lines. Consider data ((D', D''), u), where:
- D', D'' are gauges in T', T'';
- u is a point of the contracted product ∂D' ∧^U ∂D'' ≅ Isom_U(∂D'^-, ∂D''), i.e. an orientation-reversing rotation-equivariant identification of the boundary circles.
Such data is equivalent to a pair (v, D'), where v ∈ (T'⊗_C T'')^* is nondegenerate (a 'duality' between T' and T'') and D' is a gauge in T'. Equivalently one can take (v, D'').
- From (v, D'): D'' is the polar of D' with respect to v, and u is the identification x' ↦ x'' with v(x', x'') = 1.
- Conversely, u determines v by setting v = 1 on the graph of u.
Dimension check: 1 + 1 + 1 = 2 + 1 real parameters, which is consistent.

Geometrically, T', T'' are the tangent lines at two points (or punctures) to be glued. Cutting out discs and identifying the boundary circles by the inversion z·w = v^{-1} is the standard 'plumbing' (node-smoothing) construction. The gluing parameter is a point of the C^*-torsor of dualities between the tangent lines, plus a choice of radius. This is a coordinate-free formulation of plumbing.
errors: The chain of '≃' mixes levels. ∂D'∧^U∂D'' and Isom_U(∂D'^-,∂D'') are U-torsors, whereas Isom(T'^∨,T''), nondegenerate Bil(T'×T'') and the dualities form C^*-torsors. They are not isomorphic as written. Only the final assertion (u together with both gauges ⇔ a duality v together with one gauge) is correct.
Writing 'Bil(T'⊗T'')' should presumably be bilinear forms on T'×T'' (= (T'⊗T'')^*), restricted to the nondegenerate ones.
Notation T^∨ ≅ T̄ holds only after choosing the Hermitian (unitary) structure. The page is aware of this ('i.e. avec iso T ≃ T^∨') but uses the identification loosely.

ideas.what: Equivalence of categories: oriented circle-torsors under U ↔ oriented Euclidean planes ↔ unitary complex lines; U-torsors ↔ complex lines with a gauge (disc)
ideas.modern_name: U(1)-torsors / Hermitian line bundles over a point; boundary of the unit disc

ideas.what: Gauges on a complex line form an R_{>0}-torsor; duality gives an anti-isomorphism J(T) → J(T^∨)
Gluing data for two punctures (two gauged tangent lines plus an orientation-reversing identification of boundary circles) ⇔ a nondegenerate pairing v ∈ (T'⊗T'')^* plus one radius
ideas.modern_name: plumbing / node-smoothing parameter in T'⊗T'' (tangent spaces of the two branches); sewing of Riemann surfaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kra, Earle–Marden, Fay, Wolpert (plumbing); Deligne–Mumford (smoothing parameter in T_p⊗T_q); Segal (sewing, 1987–88); Vafa, Huang
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions surgery/gluing of surfaces and Teichmüller towers only in general terms

missed.claim: Grothendieck, around 1983–84, formulates the gluing of conformal surfaces along circles canonically. The plumbing parameter is a point of the C^*-torsor of dualities between the two tangent lines, plus a gauge. This is the intrinsic form of the sewing data later central to Segal's axioms for conformal field theory and to Huang's vertex operator algebra geometry.
missed.quote: revient à la donnée d'une v ∈ (T'⊗_C T'')^* i.e. une dualité entre T', T'', plus une jauge D' dans T'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck's 'chirurgie conforme' (the Teichmüller-tower program) contained the coordinate-free plumbing/sewing formalism independently of, and before, Segal's CFT. This is a historical credit point rather than a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary and the plumbing parameter in T'⊗T'' was already known (Deligne–Mumford, Kra and others). The interest is mainly historical: an intrinsic sewing formalism within Grothendieck's surgery program, predating Segal.
transcription_corrections: Top margin likely: 'torseurs sous groupes topologiques isomorphes à R/Z (resp. R)', with sense uncertain for the second.
'terme des jauges sur D = D/TU' is likely 'l'ensemble des jauges sur D = (D∖0)/U', with 'J(D) ≃ J(D^∨)°' meaning an antiisomorphism of R^{+*}-torsors (margin).
'Bil(T'⊗T'')' should likely read Bil(T',T'') / (T'⊗T'')^*. 'T'^*⊗_{C^*}T''^*' probably denotes a contracted product of C^*-torsors.
'droites vectorielles complexes munies d'une jauge conforme fixée D': 'jauge' replaces a struck-out 'distance'.
